content: The hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 plays a significant role in the metabolism of netupitant, a component of the netupitant/palonosetron combination. Below are detailed interactions and recommendations for co-administration with other drugs: 1. Cobicistat: Increases netupitant/palonosetron levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. No dosage adjustment is required, but close monitoring is recommended. 2. Conivaptan: Elevates netupitant/palonosetron levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 3. Daridorexant: Co-administration increases daridorexant levels. Limit daridorexant to 25 mg per night when used with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor closely. 4. Darunavir: Enhances netupitant/palonosetron levels through CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 5. Deflazacort: Co-administration increases deflazacort levels. Reduce deflazacort dose to one-third of the recommended dose when used with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor closely. 6. Diazepam (Buccal and Intranasal): Netupitant/palonosetron increases diazepam levels, potentially leading to adverse effects. Use caution and monitor for signs of toxicity. 7. Elagolix: Decreases netupitant/palonosetron levels by inducing CYP3A4. Monitor CYP3A substrates and consider dose adjustments. 8. Encorafenib: Alters CYP3A4 activity, potentially increasing toxicity or reducing efficacy of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. Use caution and monitor. 9. Fedratinib: Increases netupitant/palonosetron levels. Adjust doses of CYP3A4 substrates as needed. 10. Fenfluramine: Netupitant/palonosetron reduces fenfluramine efficacy due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Monitor closely. 11. Finerinone: Co-administration increases finerinone levels. Monitor serum potassium and adjust finerinone dosage as needed. 12. Fosamprenavir: Elevates netupitant/palonosetron levels. Use caution and monitor. 13. Gepirone: Increases gepirone levels. Reduce gepirone dose by 50% when used with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 14. Grapefruit: Enhances netupitant/palonosetron levels. Use caution and monitor. 15. Guanfacine: Co-administration increases guanfacine plasma concentrations. Reduce extended-release guanfacine dose to half the recommended dose. No specific recommendations for immediate-release guanfacine are available. 16. Ibrutinib: Increases ibrutinib levels. Reduce ibrutinib dose to 280 mg daily for B-cell malignancies or 420 mg daily for graft-versus-host disease when used with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the inhibitor. 17. Idelalisib: Enhances netupitant/palonosetron levels. Use caution and monitor. 18. Ifosfamide: Reduces ifosfamide efficacy. Use caution and monitor. 19. Imatinib: Increases netupitant/palonosetron levels. Use caution and monitor. 20. Indinavir: Elevates netupitant/palonosetron levels. Use caution and monitor. 21. Isavuconazonium sulfate: Increases netupitant/palonosetron levels. Use caution and monitor. 22. Isoniazid: Enhances netupitant/palonosetron levels. Use caution and monitor. 23. Istradefylline: Increases CYP3A4 substrate levels. Consider dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. 24. Itraconazole: Elevates netupitant/palonosetron levels. Use caution and monitor. 25. Ivacaftor: Increases ivacaftor levels. Reduce ivacaftor dose when co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 26. Ivosidenib: Enhances ivosidenib levels, increasing the risk of QTc prolongation. Monitor closely for QTc interval prolongation. 27. Ketoconazole: Increases netupitant/palonosetron levels. Use caution and monitor. 28. Larotrectinib: Elevates netupitant/palonosetron levels. Use caution and monitor. 29. Lefamulin: Increases lefamulin levels. Monitor for adverse effects. 30. Levamlodipine: Monitor for hypotension and edema, and adjust the dose if necessary. 31. Levo-ketoconazole: Enhances netupitant/palonosetron levels. Use caution and monitor. 32. Lopinavir: Increases netupitant/palonosetron levels. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 33. Lorlatinib: Reduces netupitant/palonosetron levels. Use caution and monitor. 34. Lumateperone: Increases lumateperone levels. Reduce lumateperone dose to 21 mg daily when co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 35. Mavacamten: Co-administration increases mavacamten levels. Reduce mavacamten dose when initiating moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 36. Mavorixafor: Enhances mavorixafor levels. Monitor for adverse effects and reduce the daily dose if necessary. 37. Naldemedine: Increases naldemedine levels. Monitor for potential adverse effects. 38. Nefazodone: Elevates netupitant/palonosetron levels. Use caution and monitor. 39. Nelfinavir: Increases netupitant/palonosetron levels. Use caution and monitor. 40. Nicardipine: Enhances netupitant/palonosetron levels. Use caution and monitor. 41. Norgestrel: Co-administration increases systemic norgestrel concentrations, potentially leading to adverse effects. Use caution and monitor. 42. Palbociclib: Increases palbociclib levels. Use caution and monitor. 43. Palovarotene: Avoid co-administration with moderate CYP3A inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce palovarotene dose by 50%. 44. Posaconazole: Elevates netupitant/palonosetron levels. Use caution and monitor. 45. Quinidine: Increases netupitant/palonosetron levels. Use caution and monitor. 46. Ribociclib: Enhances netupitant/palonosetron levels. Use caution and monitor. 47. Rimegepant: Avoid repeating rimegepant dose within 48 hours when co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 48. Ritonavir: Increases netupitant/palonosetron levels. Use caution and monitor. 49. Rucaparib: Enhances netupitant/palonosetron levels. Adjust CYP3A4 substrate dosages as needed. 50. Seladelpar: Increases seladelpar levels. Use caution in poor CYP2C9 metabolizers co-administered with moderate/strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 51. Sonidegib: Avoid co-administration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. If unavoidable, limit inhibitor use to less than 14 days and monitor for musculoskeletal adverse reactions. 52. Sparsentan: Increases sparsentan levels. 53. Stiripentol: Alters CYP3A4 activity. Monitor co-administered CYP3A4 substrates for increased or decreased effects. 54. Sufentanil SL: Co-administration increases sufentanil plasma concentrations, potentially leading to severe respiratory depression. Use caution and monitor. 55. Tazemetostat: Reduces netupitant/palonosetron levels. Use caution and monitor. 56. Tecovirimat: Decreases netupitant/palonosetron levels. Monitor sensitive CYP3A4 substrates for effectiveness. 57. Tezacaftor: Adjust tezacaftor dosage regimen when co-administered with moderate CYP3A inhibitors. 58. Tinidazole: Increases tinidazole levels. Use caution and monitor. 59. Tipranavir: Elevates netupitant/palonosetron levels. Use caution and monitor. 60. Trabectedin: Increases trabectedin levels. Use caution and monitor. 61. Vardenafil: Reduce vardenafil dose when co-administered with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 62. Voclosporin: Enhances voclosporin levels. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 63. Voriconazole: Increases netupitant/palonosetron levels. Use caution and monitor. 64. Zanubrutinib: Reduce zanubrutinib dose to 80 mg twice daily when co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the inhibitor. 65. Acetazolamide: Increases netupitant/palonosetron levels. The clinical significance is unknown. 66. Anastrozole: Elevates netupitant/palonosetron levels. The clinical significance is unknown. 67. Cyclophosphamide: Increases netupitant/palonosetron levels. The clinical significance is unknown. 68. Danazol: Enhances netupitant/palonosetron levels. The clinical significance is unknown. 69. Drospirenone: Increases netupitant/palonosetron levels. The clinical significance is unknown. 70. Estradiol Vaginal: Elevates netupitant/palonosetron levels. The clinical significance is unknown. 71. Irinotecan: Increases irinotecan levels. The clinical significance is unknown. 72. Irinotecan Liposomal: Enhances irinotecan liposomal levels. The clinical significance is unknown. 73. Acalabrutinib: Reduce acalabrutinib dose to 100 mg daily when co-administered with moderate CYP3A inhibitors. 74. Almotriptan, Amitriptyline, Amoxapine, Citalopram, Clomipramine: Co-administration increases serotonin levels, leading to potential toxicity. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 75. Apalutamide: Strongly induces CYP3A4, reducing netupitant/palonosetron levels. Avoid or substitute alternative drugs. 76. Apomorphine: Co-administration with 5HT3 antagonists is contraindicated due to the risk of profound hypotension and loss of consciousness. 77. Atazanavir: Increases netupitant/palonosetron levels. Use caution and monitor. 78. Atogepant: Enhances atogepant levels. Use caution and monitor. 79. Avapritinib: Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Use alternative drugs. 80. Betrixaban: Reduce betrixaban dose to 80 mg once, then 40 mg daily when co-administered with P-glycoprotein inhibitors. 81. Bosentan: Strongly induces CYP3A4, reducing netupitant/palonosetron levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 82. Brexpiprazole: Reduce brexpiprazole dose to one-quarter when co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors and strong/moderate CYP2D6 inhibitors. 83. Buprenorphine (Subdermal Implant and Long-Acting Injection): Co-administration increases buprenorphine levels, potentially leading to toxicity. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 84. Cannabidiol: Consider reducing cannabidiol dose when co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 85. Capivasertib: Reduce capivasertib dose when co-administered with moderate CYP3A inhibitors. 86. Carbamazepine: Strongly induces CYP3A4, reducing netupitant/palonosetron levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 87. Cenobamate: Increases CYP3A4 substrate metabolism. Adjust doses as needed. 88. Ceritinib: Enhances netupitant/palonosetron levels. Use caution and monitor. This comprehensive list highlights the importance of monitoring and adjusting therapy when netupitant/palonosetron is co-administered with other medications, particularly those affecting CYP3A4 metabolism.
